requirement.statement: The parser SHALL accept dotted fully-qualified tag names of the form `seg(.seg)*` where each segment matches the existing identifier grammar `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*`, e.g. `<dg.materials.CrudTable #users-table>`.

case.then: Parsing SHALL succeed and the node tag SHALL be the joined string `dg.materials.CrudTable`.

case.given: A tag with an empty segment, leading dot, or trailing dot (e.g. `<a..b>`, `<.a>`, `<a.>`).
case.then: The parser SHALL raise a parse error and SHALL NOT silently truncate the tag.

case.given: A dotted-tag node combining `#id`, metadata, `{...}` attributes, `(...)` extend section, and `[...]` array body.
case.then: All sections SHALL parse exactly as they do for single-segment tags.

requirement.statement: `DataElementNode.tag` and `TextElementNode.tag` SHALL remain plain strings holding the joined dotted form; single-segment tag behavior SHALL be unchanged.

case.given: Any existing document using single-segment tags.
case.when: The full test suite runs after the change.
case.then: All existing parser/formatter/loader/import/path/mutation tests SHALL pass unchanged.

requirement.statement: Formatters SHALL print dotted tags verbatim so that parse -> stringify -> parse is stable for dotted-tag documents.

case.when: The document is stringified with the default and line-block formatters.
case.then: The output SHALL contain `<dg.materials.CrudTable` and reparsing SHALL yield an equal AST.

requirement.statement: path resolution, mutation diff/apply, and loader/import SHALL treat dotted tags as opaque tag strings with no behavior change.

case.given: Two documents differing in an attribute of a dotted-tag node.
case.when: diffNodes produces mutations and applyMutations applies them.
case.then: The mutation SHALL address the node correctly and the result SHALL equal the target document.

case.given: A document containing a dotted-tag node with `#id`.
case.when: XNL.path resolve/set operates on a path through that node.
case.then: Resolution SHALL behave identically to single-segment tags.
